briefing.text: On News, Information Technology still leads (buzz 82.4, down 4.0 on the day, flat over the week, mentions down 75%; NVDA, MSFT, AMD, CRWV, AVGO), while Financials fell furthest (buzz 66.5, down 13.9; BAC, UBS, BLK) and Energy dropped 11.3 (XOM, ENB). On X, Information Technology is also first (buzz 93.0, down 0.5, mentions down 5%; NVDA, MU, AMD), with small buzz gains in Healthcare (+12.7, sentiment 0.63, WWB) and Financial Services (+11.0, BITW). On Reddit, Information Technology leads at 93.8 (down 1.1, mentions down 56%, sentiment -0.03; NVDA, MSFT, TSM), Financial Services gained 2.1 (up 10.0 on the week; fund tickers like FSKAX), and Health Care fell 3.7 (LLY, NVO). Sentiment is near neutral everywhere.

DPZ #1: 5 articles, 2 positive, but the headlines are generic analyst-upgrade roundups, so the news does not explain the rank.
TAP #3: MarketBeat notes a consensus 'Reduce' rating from 18 brokerages; routine, not a driver.
PDD #4: a piece on Temu's EUR 3 parcel duty and margins; earnings are on 11-19, which fits the rank.
SCHW #5: 14 articles, mostly bank-stock watchlists; weak explanation of the rank.
UAL #6: 23 articles, 4 negative, about US air travel disruption entering a third day; this explains the attention.
BTI #7: dividend-yield stories on falling cigarette volumes, mildly positive; partly explains it.
DIS #9: reports that new CEO Josh D'Amaro plans thousands of job cuts ahead of earnings on 11-17; explains the rank.
HD #10: coverage of Home Depot and peers reporting earnings (11-17); explains the rank.

DPZ ranks first (score 0.948) mainly on attention: Reddit/News attention is 2.37 times normal and X attention 2.91 times, both at the top percentile, with a 1.4-sigma price move (+2.5%) and a Kalshi foot-traffic market as catalyst. SHAK is second (0.899) on X attention 2.70 times normal and attention 2.03 times, a +3.2% move and a Kalshi foot-traffic market, with no news in the file. TAP is third (0.841) on X attention 1.96 times and overall attention 1.45 times normal, a +3.2% move, and an active Miller Lite point-of-sale market. For all three, volume is near or below normal, so the ranks come from attention rather than trading volume. This is the first pull in this run's state, so there is no momentum history yet.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
